messages:
maria: Heads-up — starting a latency-steering rollout for EU customer traffic that sometimes spikes at the tail. Plan: route 10% of EU production traffic to US staging pool (nearest low-cost region) for 30m canary, 90% stays in EU primary. Goal: validate p95 reduction without overloading NAT/Gateways.

kevin: Quick q — what's our DNS TTL and fail-open behavior for this? DNS churn could make things worse.

maria: TTL=30s for the canary, health-probe interval=5s (LB target group). We intentionally keep TTL low to accelerate rollback, but yes it increases lookups. Fail-open: if we lose health signals for steering controller, traffic pins back to EU primary within 60s.

ops-bot: [bot] created steering-rollout/1752709123, canary window=00:30:00, targets=[eu:90, us-canary:10] :rocket:

alex: FYI saw NAT SNAT port exhaustion in us-canary last week — ephemeral ports peaked at ~85% during burst test. If we start sending 10% prod there, watch SNAT usage closely or you'll see TCP resets. Suggest enabling per-subnet autoscaling + extra NAT capacity.

jules: Alternative: use ALB weighted target groups (layer 7) + CloudFront origin failover for some traffic rather than DNS steering. Less DNS churn and we can shift weights at the LB level. Example weight change CLI: 
```
redwood infra set-steering --from eu --weights eu=90,us-canary=10 --health-probe 5s
```
This updates LB weights atomically.

kevin: Cost heads-up — cross-region egress is ~ $0.09/GB. At 10% of traffic that could add $2k-5k/mo depending on request size. Can we estimate before enabling?

maria: I ran a quick projection: at current token throughput, 10% -> ~1.8TB/mo egress -> ~$162/mo. But if we hit retries from SNAT issues costs + latency will balloon. We'll gate on egress delta and NAT port metrics.

sre-oncall: Rollback triggers proposal: if p95 latency increases >15% over baseline OR 5xx rate >0.5% sustained for 5m OR NAT ephemeral port usage >90% on any canary subnet -> automatic rollback to 100% eu. Also manual kill switch: `infra steer rollback 1752709123`.

kevin: Can we add jittered backoff for DNS rollouts to avoid simultaneous reconnections? Also set circuit-breaker so clients don't retry aggressively.

maria: Yep — adding randomized drain windows (2-10s) per node and client-side retry 3 -> 2 with exponential backoff. We'll also enable connection re-use to reduce ephemeral port pressure.

jules: Monitoring checklist for canary (will create dashboard): p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, DNS lookup rate, NAT port usage, per-region egress GB, LB target healthy count, error logs sample.

alex: I'll pre-scale NAT gateways in us-canary and add an alert when ephemeral ports >75% so we can up-scale before hitting 90%.

maria: Launching canary in 5m. Please standby on alerts. If you want to follow along: dashboard link -> https://console.internal/redwood/steering/1752709123 (will post updates). :eyes:

kevin: ACK — watching egress and p95.

sre-oncall: If any auto-rollback happens, ops-bot will post the event and runbook pointer: /runbooks/steering-canary.md

maria: Post-mortem note: after canary we'll evaluate whether DNS TTL should go to 15s for faster churn or keep 30s to reduce lookup QPS. Decision will depend on how stable LB health signals are.

ops-bot: [bot] canary started @1752709130

maria: Thanks all. I'll update thread with metrics at +10m and +30m.
